title: Hook installation is a per-agent merge, idempotent on script filename

live_chain.title: D1 - Cursor retrieval uses sessionStart, not beforeSubmitPrompt
live_chain.body: - D: Wire Cursor's retrieval reminder to `sessionStart` with `additional_context`. - R: Cursor's `beforeSubmitPrompt` can only allow/deny submission; it cannot inject context. `sessionStart`'s `additional_context` is the documented context-injection field. - A: `beforeSubmitPrompt` — rejected, no context injection. - F: `memory_seed/seed/.memory-seed/hooks/memory-retrieval-check.py`, `memory_seed/core.py`.

live_chain.title: D1 - Script filename as the stable identifier for hook upsert
live_chain.body: - D: Detect "our" hook entry by checking if the command string contains the script filename (e.g., `session-log-check.py`), not by exact command match. - R: The script filename doesn't change between versions. Flags added to the command (the most likely version bump) would cause an exact-match check to miss, appending a duplicate. The filename check survives that. - A: Version-stamp comments inside hook entries — rejected, would require non-standard comment fields in JSON. - F: `_merge_grouped_hook`, `_merge_cursor_event_hook` (both now take `script_name` param).

live_chain.title: D2 - Multi-agent wiring reuses the existing merge framework; Copilot added as 5th agent
live_chain.body: - D: Wired the hook through `core.py` via the existing `_merge_grouped_hook` (Claude/Codex/Gemini `SessionStart`) and `_merge_cursor_event_hook` (Cursor `sessionStart`), registered in both init/update orchestration lists. Added Copilot: `_merge_copilot_mcp` writes repo-local `.github/mcp.json` (`type:local`, `tools:["*"]`), `_merge_copilot_startup_hook` writes `.github/hooks/memory-seed.json` with a **static `prompt`-type** sessionStart hook. - R: The merge framework already proved the per-agent pattern; new wiring is additive and idempotent. Copilot's MCP is repo-local (`.github/mcp.json`), fitting the project-scoped pattern. - A: A `--copilot` branch on the python script — rejected: Copilot **command** hooks cannot inject context at sessionStart (stdout consumed, not processed); only a `prompt` hook injects. So Copilot gets a static directive (must glob the dir itself), strictly weaker than the other four. - F: `memory_seed/core.py` (SeedFile entry, startup command constants, Copilot constants, 6 merge fns, both orchestration lists). - T: Dogfooded `memory-seed update` on this repo → `.claude/settings.json` gains `SessionStart` with Stop/UserPromptSubmit unchanged; `.github/mcp.json` + `.github/hooks/memory-seed.json` created; `doctor` healthy.

summary.decision: Hook configuration is merged per agent across their dedicated config files, with idempotent updates based on script filename matching rather than full command strings. The system supports five agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot), each with agent-specific configuration locations, and unconditionally installs hooks for selected agents.
summary.why: Merging preserves existing project configuration that copying would destroy. Script filename matching survives version bumps where full command comparison would leave stale entries beside new ones. The sessionStart hook injection point was chosen because beforeSubmitPrompt hooks cannot inject context. Unconditional installation keeps the system model-agnostic rather than betting on which agent a contributor uses. Copilot receives a static prompt-type hook rather than a command hook due to its architectural constraints around stdout handling.
summary.evolution: Started with sessionStart as the reliable context-injection point for Cursor, replacing beforeSubmitPrompt which lacked injection capability (ms-5e1a9d44:d1). Established script filename as the stable update key to survive version changes and flag additions (ms-7b3f1e92:d1). Generalized the merge framework to multiple agents by wiring through core.py's existing merge functions, adding Copilot as a fifth agent with different hook constraints (ms-5e366ef4:d2).

live_chain.title: D1 - Bring the roadmap and the inbox back into truth
live_chain.body: - D: Rewrote `0_NEXT_STEPS.md` against `CHANGELOG.md` and code rather than its own prior claims: Constitution v1.2 → v1.3 in all three header positions, a new "Shipped 2026-07-18/19" block, and the B2 sentence split so Trail/search parity reads as substantially closed while Storybook, Playwright and accessibility stay open. Added an "Unscoped discoveries" section and a P1 entry for a verified data-loss bug. Triaged the inbox three ways per JNL: the Living Archive proposal promoted to `2_Todo` blocked on its own section 14 decisions; both proposal sets held with disposition deferred and step 1 of the assessment's corrected sequence executed instead as an 82-row capability crosswalk; seven raw mood-board captures archived to `4_Reference/archived` with an `extracted_into` carrier, the five mockups staying where live documents cite them. - R: The roadmap was dated 2026-07-17 and knew nothing of the MCP write surface, Constitution v1.3, or the Trail UI tranche — the document that tells the next sprint what is true was the least true thing in the repo. The split matters more than the update: bundling four open items into one sentence made a closed one invisible and kept three looking closer than they are. - A: JNL chose the crosswalk over superseding the two sets outright. The 2026-07-16 precedent (de-number → rename → `7_Superseded`) would have applied, but the live 2026-07-18 decision (`mse_7e4ys7htsj90qv2c`) gates promotion on a crosswalk and had not been superseded; executing its step 1 honours it rather than routing around it. The crosswalk disproved one of the overlap hypotheses it was given — A4/B5 share no mechanism — which is the point of checking owner documents instead of the proposals' self-description. Rewrote the promoted doc's `sources:` paths even though nothing validates them: `_parse_frontmatter_scalars` skips list items, so they would have rotted silently, unlike the five mockup image links which are a hard `docs check` gate. - F: `docs/2_Todo/0_NEXT_STEPS.md`, `docs/1_Inbox/INBOX-CAPABILITY-CROSSWALK.md`, `docs/2_Todo/memory-trace-living-archive-and-editorial-focus-proposal.md`, `docs/4_Reference/archived/trace-humanised-dashboard-captures.md`, `docs/README.md`, lane READMEs. - T: `docs check` OK across 165 files (zero errors), `docs index --check` current, `links check` OK, 626 tests passed.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Answered section 14 of the Living Archive proposal: three decisions taken, three deliberately deferred. **Taken** — generated briefs are ephemeral by default and exportable only on explicit request; the **Decision Brief** is the first brief to build; adoption as the B0b visual target is gated on a task-completion test recorded inside `memory-quality-metrics-v0-proposal.md`. **Deferred** — both naming questions (§14.1–2) until a first brief exists to name, and the Pro/BYOK boundary (§14.3). The Community Decision Brief slice is now unblocked; sections 5 and 9 stay parked. - R: Each answer is grounded in something that already ships rather than in preference. Ephemeral persistence follows Invariant #6 — a generated brief is not authored memory, so caching it in-repo would create the second source of truth the invariant forbids, and an explicit export makes the user the author of anything that survives. The Decision Brief is the only candidate whose fields already exist in every entry: §4.2 maps "Why" to `R:`, "Alternatives" to `A:`, "Evidence" to `T:` plus commits, and "Related memory" to canonical graph edges, all of which the Entry Reader already renders — so it tests the reading experience rather than a data-collection change. The task-completion test exists because the capability crosswalk found nothing measures whether a grounded decision was reached: quality-v0 measures corpus health, `ranking-ab` measures ordering. - A: Rejected the Open Questions Brief as first, despite being the highest-value if it worked — the crosswalk classified an open-questions lens as a genuine delta, so nothing addresses an open question to an entry today and §4.2 forbids inferring them; it would test two unproven things at once. Rejected a preference/comprehension rating for §14.6: a warmer visual design reliably wins preference tests regardless of whether comprehension improved. Deferring §14.3 is the load-bearing choice — it *is* the commercialisation question, and this proposal cites the deferred commercialisation report as a source, so answering it would have un-deferred that by the back door rather than by decision. The test lands inside the existing memory-quality owner plan rather than beside it, per the inbox assessment's doctrine of merging deltas into existing owners instead of opening parallel programmes. - F: `docs/2_Todo/memory-trace-living-archive-and-editorial-focus-proposal.md`, `docs/2_Todo/0_NEXT_STEPS.md`, `docs/2_Todo/README.md`. - T: `docs check` OK across 165 files, `docs index --check` current after regeneration.

live_chain.title: D1 - Retire both proposal sets; the crosswalk becomes the surviving record
live_chain.body: - D: Moved all 14 documents to `7_Superseded/`, de-numbered and renamed `-exploration` per the 2026-07-16 precedent, each carrying YAML `superseded_by` pointing at [the capability crosswalk](../1_Inbox/INBOX-CAPABILITY-CROSSWALK.md). The inbox now holds two assessment artifacts and one design-reference folder; no proposal awaits triage. Both `SIDE_FOLDER_ALLOWLIST` entries were removed from `docs_check.py` and `docs/README.md`. - R: The crosswalk had already adjudicated all 82 claims and is more accurate than the sources, which systematically understate shipped capability — the Evidence Pack, typed `supersedes`/`evolves`, and blended retrieval are all described as absent by proposals that predate them. A6 and B1 are the same document written twice. Keeping 14 stale documents drafted against a pre-v1.2 Constitution, so they could be re-read, was strictly worse than keeping one corrected distillation. - A: Used YAML frontmatter for `superseded_by` rather than the precedent's bold-text `**Superseded by:**`. The precedent's style is invisible to `docs_check.py` and is precisely why several of the 12 outstanding `missing-superseded-by` warnings exist; following it would have added 14 more to a backlog already queued for repair. Verified: warnings held at 12 after the move. Rejected deleting anything — supersede-don't-delete, as with every prior set. - F: `docs/7_Superseded/` (14 added), `docs/1_Inbox/` (2 folders removed), `memory_seed/docs_check.py`, `docs/README.md`, `tests/test_docs_check.py`. - T: `docs check` OK across 165 files, zero errors; warnings unchanged at 12 + 16; `docs index --check` current; 627 tests pass. 30 references were rewritten — 28 in the crosswalk plus 2 in the inbox README — and 22 intra-set sibling links that only broke once the files became siblings in a new lane.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: JNL asked to triage the Inbox and fold it into a coherent next-steps plan. Checked `docs/1_Inbox/` - already marked "TRIAGED 2026-07-20, no untriaged proposals remain" by an earlier session today, holding only two evaluation docs (`INBOX-ASSESSMENT.md`, `INBOX-CAPABILITY-CROSSWALK.md`) and one design-reference folder (`trace-humanised-dashboard-references/`). JNL then asked the sharper question directly: if these are already folded into 0_NEXT_STEPS.md, why are they still physically sitting in `1_Inbox/` rather than their canonical lane? Correct per the project's own rule (`docs/README.md`): `1_Inbox/` holds raw, untriaged captures; `4_Reference/` holds source material. All three items were fully evaluated (the crosswalk is "the surviving record" other documents cite; the mockups folder's themes are already extracted and it's actively cited by the Living Archive proposal in `2_Todo/`) - neither fits "untriaged." `2_Todo/` was considered and rejected as the destination: that lane is for active work carrying `priority`/`next_action`, and the actual work item consuming the mockups (the Living Archive proposal) already correctly lives there - the mockups themselves are reference material for that work, not a work item in their own right. - R: Moved all three (`git mv`) to `docs/4_Reference/`. Fixed every citing link: 14 `7_Superseded/` `superseded_by`/prose pointers to the crosswalk (2 also referenced the assessment doc), 3 `2_Todo/` plans (`0_NEXT_STEPS.md`, `memory-quality-metrics-v0-proposal.md`, `memory-seed-semantic-record-and-signal-foundation-plan.md`), the Living Archive proposal's 5 mockup image embeds plus its `sources:` pointer, the reciprocal links between the mockups folder and its already-archived raw-capture sibling (both directions - the folder's depth changed from 2-under-a-lane to 1-under-a-lane, so `../../4_Reference/archived/...` became `../archived/...` and vice versa), `docs_check.py`'s `SIDE_FOLDER_ALLOWLIST` (moved the `trace-humanised-dashboard-references` entry from `1_Inbox` to `4_Reference`) and its test, `docs/README.md`'s hand-written allowlist table, and a full rewrite of `docs/1_Inbox/README.md` (now genuinely empty - zero documents of any kind, not just zero untriaged proposals). Left one pre-existing, unrelated issue alone: two `sources:` pointers in the Living Archive proposal to the retired proposal-set index files at their old pre-supersession paths - stale from the 2026-07-20 retirement, not enforced by `docs check` (frontmatter list items aren't link-checked), out of scope for this move. - F: `docs/1_Inbox/README.md`, `docs/2_Todo/0_NEXT_STEPS.md`, `docs/2_Todo/memory-quality-metrics-v0-proposal.md`, `docs/2_Todo/memory-seed-semantic-record-and-signal-foundation-plan.md`, `docs/2_Todo/memory-trace-living-archive-and-editorial-focus-proposal.md`, `docs/4_Reference/INBOX-ASSESSMENT.md` (moved), `docs/4_Reference/INBOX-CAPABILITY-CROSSWALK.md` (moved), `docs/4_Reference/trace-humanised-dashboard-references/` (moved, 6 files), `docs/4_Reference/archived/trace-humanised-dashboard-captures.md`, 14 `docs/7_Superseded/*.md` files plus their `README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `memory_seed/docs_check.py`, `tests/test_docs_check.py`. - T: `docs index` regenerated the 4 marker-scoped lane tables (1_Inbox 2->0, 4_Reference 14->16). `docs check` - "Docs lifecycle OK (166 file(s) checked)", 16 pre-existing warnings, no new ones. `links check` - "Session memory integrity OK". `pytest tests/test_docs_check.py tests/test_docs_index.py` - 26/26. Full `pytest tests` - 641 passed, 14 subtests passed (the +2 over this session's earlier 639 baseline is the concurrent background session's own merged `SEED_FILES`/registry parity test, unrelated to this change). Merged `claude/docs/inbox-to-reference-move` to main, branch deleted.

summary.decision: Inbox items are promoted conservatively based on evidence of actionability; overlapping proposals are consolidated into a single capability crosswalk that supersedes individual sources, with every workstream assigned exactly one owner to prevent competing contracts. Assessment artifacts are classified as reference material, not inbox items, because the inbox holds untriaged captures while reference holds source material that feeds active work.
summary.why: The inbox accumulated stale, overlapping proposals drafted against outdated assumptions. A distilled crosswalk proved more accurate than the sources, which systematically understated shipped capability. One active owner per workstream prevents duplicate lifecycle tracking, makes dependencies explicit, and renders the roadmap trustworthy. Moving assessment documents to reference removes inbox ambiguity: documents fully evaluated against project lanes belong to reference, while only raw, untriaged captures belong to inbox.
summary.evolution: Established conservative triage criteria, promoting only actionable items with evidence (mse_d2daxtnv8eqx4vqr:d1). Sequenced platform ideas with explicit gates after React Trail parity (mse_mazbt6cek8m8a6st:d1). Unified workstream ownership to prevent competing contracts and explicit dependencies (mse_ddba1ztxqhasfbwf:d2). Rewrote the roadmap document against live code and CHANGELOG, introducing the capability crosswalk as the surviving record and retiring overlapping proposals (mse_wjntbg88n3m0qjss:d1, mse_tx1c338ca1ybr666:d1). Answered Living Archive proposal section 14 selectively, deferring naming and commercialisation questions (mse_y9q4bnv2yckk6w74:d1). Moved triaged assessment artifacts to reference lane, leaving inbox empty (mse_2geqfa8tg182a77p:d1).

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Implemented P0.1 of the configurable integration-mode feature: the setting + core reader + `esr` surfacing. `memory_seed/core.py` gains `INTEGRATION_MODES = ("local-merge", "pr")`, `DEFAULT_INTEGRATION_MODE = "local-merge"`, and `read_integration_mode(target_root)` - a fail-open stdlib line-scanner (same style as `read_project_agents`/`read_project_participants`, no YAML dep) reading a top-level `integration_mode:` scalar from `.memory-seed/project.yaml`. `memory_seed/esr.py` carries the active mode on `EsrReport` (+ `to_dict`) and prints a new `## Integration mode` section. - R: Fail-open to `local-merge` on an absent file/key, an unreadable file, or an unrecognised value keeps every legacy/unconfigured project behaving exactly as today - the field is purely additive. Surfacing the mode each preflight makes it visible which integration flow is in effect (local-merge = `session merge-branch` into local main, no push; pr = push + PR). This is the foundation the OpenSSF PR-flow step consumes (declares `pr`). - F: `memory_seed/core.py` (constants + `read_integration_mode`), `memory_seed/esr.py` (`EsrReport.integration_mode` + `to_dict` + `## Integration mode` section + `read_integration_mode` wiring), `tests/test_memory_seed.py` (+1 reader test), `tests/test_esr.py` (+1 surfacing test, section-presence list extended). - T: core 424 passed. Reader test covers absent-file/absent-key/pr/local-merge/garbage-fail-open/ quoted; esr test covers the default and a declared `pr`. The `esr` CLI on this repo (no field set) prints "Integration mode: local-merge — integrate via session merge-branch … no push."

summary.decision: integration_mode is a project-local configuration setting read from .memory-seed/project.yaml as a scalar field, determining whether changes integrate via local-merge or PR. The default is local-merge, applied fail-open when the file, field, or value is absent or unrecognised.
summary.why: Fail-open behavior keeps every legacy or unconfigured project unchanged, making the setting purely additive. Surfacing the active mode in ESR preflights makes it visible which integration flow is in effect. The setting is foundation for downstream features like OpenSSF PR-flow requirements and agent contracts that honor the chosen mode.
summary.evolution: Implemented the feature in a single tranche (mse_t388apx6evvmmd1r:d1) with core reader using the same fail-open stdlib line-scanner style as existing project metadata readers, DEFAULT_INTEGRATION_MODE constant, and ESR surfacing in a new Integration mode section.

title: Link audit writes inert stubs; only an approval turns one into an edge

live_chain.title: D1 - Lifecycle-link authoring assist
live_chain.body: - D: Proposed `docs/1_Inbox/lifecycle-link-authoring-assist-proposal.md`: a `link audit --date <d> --apply` that scaffolds the dated link sidecar with inert, machine-detectable `classify_pending` stubs (entry_id + commented candidate evidence) the author resolves into a real supersedes/evolves edge; a `links check` `sidecar-unclassified-stub` warning + an `esr` stub count so open stubs can't be forgotten; plus an optional advisory commit-time nudge and a deferred MCP `memory_link_record`. - R: The user asked how lifecycle links get updated and whether a background hook does it. Grounded the answer - no background process: `link audit` is read-only by design, edges are hand-authored into `.memory-seed/sessions/links/YYYY-MM/*.md` and unioned at read time. The friction is that hand-authoring (path / frontmatter / yaml shape / chronology), the same drop-or-malform failure the entry-format lint just closed for entries. Retrieved the why first (`mse_8wq2vnr5tkxm3jhc`): classification is a deliberate author judgment and the candidate set is intentionally file/topic-based (no all-pairs scan), so the proposal removes MECHANICAL friction only - it never auto-classifies or writes a live edge. - F: docs/1_Inbox/lifecycle-link-authoring-assist-proposal.md

live_chain.title: D2 - Link-audit stubs created for 2026-07-28 (missed) and 2026-07-29 (today); five upgrade candidates flagged for JNL, none applied without approval
live_chain.body: - D: Ran `memory-seed link audit --date 2026-07-28 --apply` (7 inert stubs) and `--date 2026-07-29 --apply` (2 inert stubs) - mechanical, safe, no live edge written by either. Read the candidate lists and picked out five where the litmus ("refines while it stays valid -> evolves") reads clearly rather than coincidental shared-file overlap: the declared-axis entry over the topic-sidecar-authority entries; the crossing-avoidance entry over the chain-spiral entry (same simulation, extends it) and over the related-chain-kind entry (the tool itself flagged "already related - consider upgrading"); and the open-external-folder entry over the prior worktree-navigation-contract entry (directly extends the same allowlist mechanism). Presented to JNL for approval; not converted to live edges in this entry. - R: `end_of_turn.md`'s Lifecycle Link Sweep step is explicit that stub creation is mechanical/safe but converting a stub to a live edge needs human approval - "ask the user for approval before converting any stub into a live edge (same gate as persona evolution), showing the evidence and proposed classification." The other candidates in both dates' stub lists were left unresolved rather than forced into a relationship, per the skill's own instruction that shared files can be coincidental. - A: Auto-classify the clear-looking ones without asking - rejected, the skill names this exact gate explicitly and by name (same as persona evolution). Skip the sweep entirely since it's two days old, not one - rejected: the skill scopes the sweep to entries needing classification, not to a single calendar day, and 07-28's whole graph-navigation tranche had never been audited at all. - F: `.memory-seed/sessions/links/2026-07/2026-07-28.md` (new), `.memory-seed/sessions/links/2026-07/2026-07-29.md` (new) - both inert stub-only files. - T: `memory-seed links check` confirms both files parse as unresolved stubs, not errors.

summary.decision: The link audit writes inert stubs with machine-detected candidate edges, classified but not yet live. Only explicit human approval converts a stub into an actual edge. Negative verdicts—entries whose candidates were all judged unrelated—are recorded rather than left unexamined.
summary.why: A mechanical candidate generator should not author lineage; that remains a deliberate human act. Keeping stubs inert separates the cheap claim "might be related" from the graph claim "IS related." Recording negative verdicts distinguishes "looked and found nothing" from "never looked," both important states for maintenance and completeness.
summary.evolution: Proposed the lifecycle-link authoring assist scaffold with inert stubs containing entry_id and commented candidate evidence that authors would resolve into real edges (mse_jg33a730vpr4085a:d1). Implemented and executed the audit for two dates, creating inert stub files with classified candidates and flagging five cases where the evolves litmus read clearly, withholding approval conversion pending user decision (mse_63qcaab119xmyx0b:d2).

title: Append-only link retraction via retracts: blocks

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Added an append-only `retracts:` mechanism to link sidecars so a published lifecycle edge can be downgraded or removed without reopening the block that declared it (which the fuse forbids). A new correction block declares `retracts: <kind> <ref> [(YYYY-MM-DD)]`; the reader (`entry_link_sidecars`) unions all edges then subtracts each retracted one (entry-level by `(kind, target)`, decision by the exact 4-tuple); `links check` validates malformed / dangling (nothing to retract) / forward-only (retract cannot pre-date the edge). A downgrade is a retract of the old kind plus a fresh edge of the new kind, authored together - so `evolves` becomes `related` with no block reopened. - R: The hand-audit exposed the gap directly: `session merge-branch` rightly refused my in-place edits to published sidecar blocks (append-only), and there was no sanctioned way to reclassify an edge, so I had to bypass the guard with a plain merge (JNL kept that correction but asked for a real mechanism). This closes it - future corrections use the path the fuse already accepts (a new block). Per JNL's steer, the retract identifies its target by kind + ref and is optionally pinned by the original declaration date ("use the date and the id"). - A: A `reclassifies:` one-liner (retract-plus-readd) was considered and deferred - the explicit retract+readd pair reads clearer. Editing blocks in place (rejected: bypasses the guard) and deleting them (rejected: destroys the evidence the edge existed) were the non-append-only alternatives. - F: memory_seed/core.py (parser, validator), memory_seed/retrieval.py (reader subtraction), tests/test_links_check.py (3 cases), docs/3_Spec/draft/link-retraction.md - T: 3 new retract tests pass; full backend suite; `links check` integrity OK

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Converted the 5 hand-audit downgrades from in-place link-sidecar edits (an Invariant #2 violation) to append-only `retracts:` blocks: restored each original `evolves` edge and appended a `retracts: evolves <ref> (<date>)` + fresh `related_entries: <ref>` correction block, so the effective edge is still `related` but the history is append-only and the campaign's original claim is preserved. Also fixed a retract-reader bug the conversion exposed - an arrow-prefixed bare ref (`d2 -> X`) is collected as BOTH an entry-level edge and a source-only decision edge, so a retract must remove both twins or the decision one silently survives (pair mse_hejpp9whj0nn8jyy showed it). Added a regression test. - R: Reading `docs/CONSTITUTION.md` to update its durable facts surfaced that the earlier plain-merge of the in-place downgrades (`ea29bcc`) rewrote PUBLISHED link sidecars - exactly what Invariant #2 (append-only) forbids, and the v1.4 amendment log explicitly walls link sidecars off from in-place editing (citing the same fuse refusal I bypassed). At the time neither JNL nor I framed it as a constitutional violation and JNL said "keep it as is" - but that was before the sanctioned `retracts:` mechanism existed. Presented the finding; JNL chose to convert. This restores the corpus to Invariant #2 compliance and makes the pending docs honest. The twin fix is required for the conversion to actually complete each downgrade. - A: Leave the in-place edits and document the exception (rejected by JNL in favour of compliance). git-revert the audit merge (rejected: messier than a targeted restore + retract, and would not add the retract blocks the append-only path needs). - F: .memory-seed/sessions/links/2026-07/{2026-07-03,05,12,16,17}.md (restore evolves + retract block); memory_seed/retrieval.py (twin-retract fix); tests/test_links_check.py (twin regression test) - T: 4 retract tests (incl. new twin case); reader confirms all 5 downgrades now `related` not `evolves`; `links check` integrity OK

summary.decision: Published lifecycle edges are never edited in place. A downgrade or removal is expressed by appending a new sidecar block declaring `retracts: <kind> <ref> [(date)]`; the reader unions all edges then subtracts the retracted ones, and `links check` validates violations. A downgrade combines a retract of the old kind with a fresh edge of the new kind in a single authored block.
summary.why: The session's fuse forbids reopening published blocks, so correction must append rather than edit. The retraction mechanism makes the change non-destructive and auditable—the history shows both the original edge and the correction. The twin-retract fix ensures that multi-form edges (arrow-prefixed refs appearing as both entry-level and decision-level) are completely removed. The conversion of five hand-audited downgrades from in-place edits restored constitutional compliance with Invariant #2 (append-only).
summary.evolution: The initial mechanism allowed retracting edges by kind and ref, optionally pinned by the original declaration date. Then the mechanism was applied retroactively to fix five published sidecar edits that violated the append-only invariant, surfacing and fixing a bug where arrow-prefixed bare refs survived as decision-level edges even when their entry-level twins were retracted.
